standard.title: Investigate dance across cultures and contexts
standard.description: investigate ways that dance works, performers and/or choreographers across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts use the elements of dance, choreographic devices and/or production elements to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify how elements of dance and choreographic devices are used to communicate ideas (AC9ADA6E01). They have not yet investigated how cultural, historical and contextual factors shape these choices across diverse dance traditions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how elements of dance, choreographic devices and production elements are used across cultures, times and contexts to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning.

nodes.label: Identifying elements and devices in dance works
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify elements of dance and choreographic devices in a given work and describe how each contributes to the meaning communicated
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two elements of dance or choreographic devices in a given work; describe how each contributes to the meaning or effect
nodes.typical_width: Analyse a range of dance works to identify elements and devices; explain how specific choices communicate intended ideas or perspectives
wider: Compare how the same element of dance (e.g. repetition, use of space) is used in two works from different genres or cultural contexts — analyse what the comparison reveals about how meaning is made differently

Use Viewpoints questions to investigate choreographic intention — 'What was the choreographer's intention?', 'What ideas did the dance express?' — and evaluate whether the choreographic choices achieve the intention
Analyse how a single realistic movement can be manipulated from representational to symbolic — investigate examples across different dance traditions

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a repertoire of dance works and the elements/devices used within them before they can reason about how context shapes meaning-making choices. A single example gives too narrow a lens for genuine comparative analysis across cultures and times.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two elements or devices in a given work
Describes how each contributes to meaning — not just names the element
Does not confuse describing what a dance looks like with explaining how it communicates

nodes.label: Investigating across cultures, times and contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how cultural, historical and contextual factors shape how elements of dance and choreographic devices are used to communicate ideas
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one dance work or choreographer whose practice is shaped by cultural or historical context; explain how context influences specific choreographic choices
nodes.typical_width: Investigate dance works across at least two different cultural or historical contexts; analyse how context shapes choreographic choices and what ideas each work communicates
wider: Investigate the development of a dance style across different social and historical contexts — analyse how social and environmental factors shaped the style's evolution
Investigate how digital tools and immersive technologies like VR are influencing contemporary choreography and performance — analyse what new expressive possibilities these technologies create
Investigate the reciprocal influence between dance traditions from different cultural contexts — analyse how cross-cultural exchange shapes dance practice

response_modes.reason: Students commonly describe what a dance work does without connecting it to cultural or historical context. Investigating works from multiple distinct cultural and historical contexts forces students to develop contextual reasoning as a habit — understanding that choreographic choices are shaped by social, historical and environmental factors, not just individual preference.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The digital/VR direction opens genuinely new territory — students who investigate how immersive technologies are reshaping choreography and performance encounter contemporary questions about what dance is and what it can communicate that go well beyond analysis of existing traditions.
success_criteria: Investigates at least one work whose choreographic choices are connected to cultural or historical context
Explains how context shapes specific element or device choices
Goes beyond surface description to explain the relationship between context and meaning

nodes.label: Connecting investigation to own choreographic practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use their investigation of dance works across contexts to inform specific decisions in their own choreography
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one specific insight from investigating other dance works that has influenced a decision in own choreography; explain the connection
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how investigating dance works across contexts informs own choreographic choices; document specific points of influence and how they are adapted rather than imitated
wider: Develop a journal documenting how investigation of diverse dance traditions has extended own choreographic vocabulary and opened new directions
Investigate how distinguishing stylistic features of specific dance genres can inform own choreography — develop a choreographic approach that is informed by but not derivative of those genres
Construct an argument about why investigating diverse dance traditions produces stronger and more distinctive choreography than drawing on a single tradition

response_modes.reason: This node requires students to bring together element/device analysis (Node 1) and contextual investigation (Node 2) and connect both to their own choreographic decisions. Students who can analyse other works but cannot use that analysis to inform own practice have not met the standard's full investigative demand.

Students commonly describe what they have investigated without articulating how it changes specific decisions in own work. Scaffolding the connection — what did I learn, what decision did it change, how is my adaptation different from imitation — builds the analytical-to-practical transfer.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one insight from investigating other works that influenced own choreography
Explains the connection — not just 'I was inspired by'
